content_voiceover: This slide continues the Z N F three eight four discussion with some newer, therapeutically relevant findings that boards may test as an emerging concept. First, there's a concerning signal that treating relapsed or refractory Z N F three eight four rearranged ALL with blinatumomab or C D nineteen C A R T-cell therapy may actually increase the risk of lineage switch, meaning the leukemia can convert from a B lymphoblastic phenotype to a myeloid phenotype under the selective pressure of C D nineteen-directed immunotherapy. This is thought to relate to the underlying biology of these blasts, which, as we just saw, already have some myeloid marker expression at baseline. Mechanistically, Z N F three eight four rearranged blasts show overexpression of F L T three and upregulation of the J A K-S T A T signaling pathway, which gives a rationale for targeted therapy. Encouragingly, gilteritinib, an F L T three inhibitor already approved in A M L, has shown significant antileukemic efficacy in patient-derived xenograft models of Z N F three eight four rearranged ALL. So the emerging clinical picture is, be cautious about C D nineteen-directed immunotherapy triggering lineage switch in this subtype, and watch for F L T three inhibitors as a potential future targeted option.
keypoints: Blinatumomab or CD19 CAR T-cell therapy may increase lineage switch risk
ZNF384-rearranged blasts overexpress FLT3 and activate JAK-STAT signaling
Gilteritinib, an FLT3 inhibitor, shows efficacy in PDX models
Consider lineage switch risk before choosing CD19-directed immunotherapy
